tests.title: Unit 8: Final Accounts of a Sole Proprietorship – Practice Test 1

questions.question_text: Final accounts are:
options: Statements prepared at the end of the period to find profit or loss and the financial position
questions.explanation: They include trading, P&L and balance sheet.

questions.question_text: The components of final accounts are:
options: Cash book, bank book and petty cash
Trading account, profit and loss account and balance sheet

questions.question_text: An objective of preparing final accounts is to:
options: Ascertain profit or loss and the financial position
questions.explanation: They also help users take decisions.

questions.question_text: The trading account is prepared to find:
questions.explanation: It shows the result of buying and selling goods.

questions.question_text: The trading account has on its debit side:
options: Opening stock, purchases and direct expenses
questions.explanation: Sales and closing stock are on the credit side.

questions.question_text: The formula for gross profit is:
options: Net sales − cost of goods sold
questions.explanation: Gross profit appears when credits exceed debits.

questions.question_text: Cost of goods sold =
options: Opening stock + net purchases + direct expenses − closing stock
questions.explanation: It is the direct cost of goods sold.

questions.question_text: Direct expenses include:
options: Wages, carriage inwards and freight inwards
questions.explanation: They are incurred up to bringing goods to a saleable condition.

questions.question_text: Indirect expenses include:
questions.explanation: They are shown in the P&L account.

questions.question_text: In the trading account, purchases returns are:
options: Deducted from purchases and sales returns from sales
questions.explanation: They give net purchases and net sales.

questions.question_text: Closing stock is shown on the:
options: Credit side of the trading account and the asset side of the balance sheet
Debit side of the trading account
questions.explanation: It reduces the cost of goods sold.

questions.question_text: Opening stock is shown on the:
options: Credit side of the trading account
Debit side of the trading account
questions.explanation: It adds to the cost of goods sold.

questions.question_text: Closing entries for the trading account transfer:
options: Nominal accounts (opening stock, purchases, sales, direct expenses) to the trading account
questions.explanation: The balance is the gross profit or loss.

questions.question_text: Gross loss arises when:
options: Debit side of the trading account exceeds the credit side
questions.explanation: Cost of goods sold exceeds sales.

questions.question_text: The gross profit ratio is:
A profit and loss account is prepared to find:
questions.explanation: It starts with gross profit from the trading account.

questions.question_text: The P&L account begins with:
options: Gross profit (credit side) or gross loss (debit side)

questions.question_text: The debit side of the P&L includes:
The credit side of the P&L includes:
options: Gross profit, other incomes and gains

questions.question_text: Selling and distribution expenses include:
options: Advertising, carriage outwards and salesmen's salary

questions.question_text: Administrative expenses include:
questions.explanation: They are incurred in running the office.

questions.question_text: Financial expenses include:
options: Interest on loans and bank charges

questions.question_text: Net profit =
options: Gross profit + other incomes − indirect expenses

questions.question_text: Net profit is transferred to:
Drawings are:
options: Not shown in the P&L; deducted from capital in the balance sheet

tests.title: Unit 8: Final Accounts of a Sole Proprietorship – Practice Test 2

questions.question_text: Interest on capital is:
options: An expense (debited to P&L) and added to capital
questions.explanation: It is a charge against profit.

questions.question_text: Interest on drawings is:
options: An income (credited to P&L) and added to drawings
questions.explanation: It is charged to the proprietor.

questions.question_text: The net profit ratio is:
A balance sheet is:
options: A statement of assets, liabilities and capital at a given date

questions.question_text: A balance sheet is:
questions.explanation: It is not part of the double entry.

questions.question_text: Marshalling is:
options: Arranging assets and liabilities in a particular order
questions.explanation: Two orders are used: liquidity and permanence.

questions.question_text: The liquidity order shows:
options: Most liquid assets first (cash), the permanence order shows fixed assets first
questions.explanation: Banks use liquidity order; companies use permanence order.

questions.question_text: Assets are classified in the balance sheet as:
The trial balance differs from the balance sheet in that the trial balance:
options: Lists all ledger balances, the balance sheet only assets, liabilities and capital
questions.explanation: The balance sheet is prepared after the P&L.

questions.question_text: The trading account differs from the P&L account in that the trading account shows:
options: Gross profit, the P&L shows net profit

questions.question_text: Closing capital =
options: Opening capital + net profit + additional capital − drawings
questions.explanation: It appears on the liabilities side.

questions.question_text: Adjusting entries are entries:
options: Passed at the year-end to record items not yet recorded, e.g., outstanding expenses and depreciation

questions.question_text: Adjustments are required to:
options: Ensure all incomes and expenses of the year are recorded (matching concept)

questions.question_text: The double effect of adjustments means they:
options: Affect both the P&L (or trading) account and the balance sheet
questions.explanation: E.g., outstanding rent is an expense and a liability.

questions.question_text: An adjustment has only a single effect when:
options: It is already deducted in the trial balance or affects only one statement
questions.explanation: E.g., closing stock given in the trial balance.

questions.question_text: Closing stock given in the adjustment is shown:
options: On the credit side of the trading account and as an asset in the balance sheet

questions.question_text: Closing stock given in the trial balance is shown:
options: On the credit of the trading account
Only in the balance sheet as an asset
questions.explanation: It has already been adjusted in purchases.

questions.question_text: Outstanding expenses are:
options: Added to the expense in the P&L and shown as a liability in the balance sheet

questions.question_text: Prepaid expenses are:
options: Deducted from the expense in the P&L and shown as an asset
questions.explanation: They are benefit of a future period.

questions.question_text: Accrued income is:
options: Added to the income in the P&L and shown as an asset

questions.question_text: Income received in advance is:
options: Deducted from income in the P&L and shown as a liability
questions.explanation: It belongs to a future period.

questions.question_text: Depreciation is:
options: Debited to P&L and deducted from the asset in the balance sheet
questions.explanation: It spreads the cost over life.

questions.question_text: Further bad debts are:
options: Debited to P&L and deducted from debtors in the balance sheet

questions.question_text: A provision for doubtful debts is:
options: Charged to the P&L and deducted from debtors in the balance sheet

questions.question_text: A provision for discount on debtors is:
options: Charged to the P&L and deducted from debtors
questions.explanation: It anticipates discount to be allowed.

tests.title: Unit 8: Final Accounts of a Sole Proprietorship – Practice Test 3

questions.question_text: A provision for discount is calculated on:
options: Debtors after deducting bad debts and provision for doubtful debts
questions.explanation: It is a percentage of good debtors.

questions.question_text: A reserve differs from a provision in that a reserve is:
options: An appropriation of profit, while a provision is a charge against profit

questions.question_text: Goods taken by the proprietor are:
options: Deducted from purchases and debited to drawings

questions.question_text: When insured goods are destroyed by fire:
options: The insurance claim admitted is shown as an asset and only the net loss is charged to P&L

questions.question_text: Outstanding interest on loan is:
options: Added to interest in the P&L and shown as a liability

Capital in the balance sheet differs from the opening capital because of:
options: Profit, additional capital and drawings during the year

questions.question_text: The balance sheet is important to lenders because it:
options: Shows the assets, liabilities and solvency of the business

questions.question_text: Final accounts are significant to tax authorities because:
options: Income tax is computed on the profit shown

questions.question_text: Final accounts help in comparison with competitors by:
A limitation of final accounts is that they:
options: Are based on historical cost and estimates and ignore non-monetary factors

questions.question_text: The accounting period concept in final accounts means:
options: Profit is measured over a defined period, usually one year

questions.question_text: The profit of a manufacturing concern differs because it prepares:
options: A manufacturing account before the trading account
questions.explanation: It shows the cost of production.

questions.question_text: The manufacturing account is prepared to find:
questions.explanation: It includes materials, labour and factory overheads.

questions.question_text: The vertical format of the balance sheet:
options: Lists assets and liabilities one below the other
questions.explanation: It is the format used by companies.
